articles.title: China targets US rare earth and other firms with export controls
articles.summary:
STORY: China added more U.S. entities to its export control list on Monday. 

It accused them of being linked to the U.S. military.

The list stops Chinese dual-use exports to the companies. 

MP Materials and USA Rare Earth as well as eight other firms were added.

The move is in retaliation for Washington placing a number of Chinese companies under restrictions last month.

The Pentagon-supported MP Materials operates the only active rare earth mine in the U.S.

And it - like USA Rare Earth - is also involved in the mine-to-magnet supply chain.

Aveox was also placed on the list.

It's a motor manufacturer for mission-critical applications.

The three U.S. companies weren't available for comment outside of business hours.

The measures are a response to what Beijing called the "U.S. government's malicious practice."

Chinese authorities said it aimed to safeguard national security and interests, and fulfill international obligations like non-proliferation.

The move amounts to a full ban on dual-use exports to the named firms, and tightens rules that previously only required export licenses.

But some analysts said China's actions were a largely symbolic response to an earlier move by the U.S.

They argue most of the companies are U.S. defense industry players and likely won't do business in China.

The Pentagon previously made its own list of Chinese tech companies it believes to be aiding the country's military.

The list was updated this month to include tech firms Alibaba and Baidu, as well as autogiants BYD and ​NIO.
